[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-abb-definition-template.md#normative-language-convention]

### Normative Language Convention

> **Authoring note — choose ONE pattern based on ABB type:**
>
> **Composite ABB**: include the full RFC 2119 table below. This section is defined once for the entire hierarchy and all Component ABBs inherit it by reference.
>
> **Component ABB**: replace this entire section with a one-liner reference back to the Vision: `Per [<GUID-SEC-*-VISION-0.N.NN> §Normative Language Convention](<relative-path-to-vision>.md): **SHALL** = mandatory; **SHOULD** = strongly recommended; **MAY** = optional.`

This document and all Component ABBs in this hierarchy use normative language per RFC 2119:

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SHALL** | Mandatory — absolute obligation |
| **SHALL NOT** | Mandatory prohibition |
| **SHOULD** | Strongly recommended — deviation requires documented justification |
| **SHOULD NOT** | Strongly discouraged — deviation requires documented justification |
| **MAY** | Optional — permitted but not required |

> **Exception and Waiver Process**: Teams that cannot meet a SHALL requirement must submit a risk acceptance or waiver request through the established enterprise governance process. Waivers require documented risk justification and approval from appropriate security leadership or designated delegate. Temporary waivers must include a remediation timeline.
